result: The new version of qFit-ligand integrates RDKit's ETKDG conformer generator for stochastic conformational sampling, which generates 5000-7000 ligand conformations and enriches low-energy conformations of small molecules and macrocycles.
evaluation: Claims C8, C9, C25, C26, C37, and C40 describe the methodological implementation of RDKit-based sampling. The integration is clearly documented in the methods, the ETKDG approach is properly cited, and the enrichment of low-energy conformations is supported by strain reduction data (C9, C50, C54).

result: In the development dataset (n=135), the new qFit-ligand improved RSCC in 83.7% of structures, EDIAm in 77.0%, and reduced torsional strain in 61.5% with a mean difference of -0.2 kcal/mol compared to modified true positive single-conformer models.
evaluation: Claims C48-C52 provide specific quantitative results from the development dataset with clear sample sizes and percentages. The improvements in RSCC, EDIAm, and strain are well-documented with statistical measures. The modified true positive approach (removing 'B' conformers) provides a reasonable baseline for comparison.

result: Compared to the prior version of qFit-ligand, the new version achieved higher RSCC in 57.8% of structures, lower strain in 68.9%, and higher EDIAm in 85.9% of the development dataset. Among structures where the prior version had higher RSCC, 67.9% had higher strain than the new version.
evaluation: Claims C53-C56 provide direct quantitative comparisons between the new and prior versions with specific percentages and sample sizes. The observation that the prior version often achieved better RSCC at the cost of higher strain (C56) demonstrates a key improvement in the new algorithm's balance between fit and physical realism.

result: Using synthetic datasets, qFit-ligand was found to perform most effectively with map resolutions better than 2.0 Å, with an occupancy detection limit around 30%.
evaluation: Claims C58 and C59 are supported by the synthetic dataset analysis showing RSCC decline at resolutions worse than 2.0 Å and increased RMSD variability at 0.80/0.20 and 0.90/0.10 occupancy splits. The synthetic dataset approach with controlled occupancies and resolutions provides appropriate evidence for these operational bounds.

result: In an unbiased dataset (n=589), qFit-ligand produced single conformers in 46.0% of structures, two conformers in 35.7%, and three conformers in 18.3%. Compared to modified true positives, 79.8% showed enhanced RSCC, 80.6% had higher EDIAm, and 55.3% had reduced strain.
evaluation: Claims C60-C65 provide comprehensive quantitative results from an independent validation dataset with appropriate filtering criteria (RMSD ≥0.2 Å, B-factor <80 Å², occupancy ≥0.3). The consistency with the development dataset results strengthens confidence in the method's generalizability.

result: In a high-strain dataset (n=191 structures with strain >10 kcal/mol), qFit-ligand modeled 75.4% with single conformers. Even without modeling alternative conformers in most structures, RSCC increased in 53.4%, EDIAm in 81.2%, and strain decreased in 66.5%.
evaluation: Claims C67-C70 demonstrate that qFit-ligand can reduce strain even when producing single-conformer models, suggesting the algorithm samples out of local minima. The high-strain dataset (>10 kcal/mol cutoff) provides an appropriate test case, though the cutoff is acknowledged as somewhat arbitrary (C66).

result: For macrocycles (n=73 analyzable structures from 150 initial), qFit-ligand improved RSCC in 69.9% of structures, EDIAm in 58.3% (for structures <2 Å resolution), and reduced strain in 57.5% with a mean difference of -0.1 kcal/mol. Lower input RSCC correlated with identification of more alternate conformers.
evaluation: Claims C74-C79 show improvements for macrocycles, but significant data loss occurred: 19.3% failed refinement (C71), 19 cases had compromised geometry (C72), and 19.3% had failed strain calculations (C73). This 51% attrition rate raises concerns about selection bias and whether the analyzable subset is representative. The authors acknowledge macrocycles suffer from refinement issues (C95-C96).

result: For fragment screening event maps (n=20), only 9 structures had RMSD <0.5 Å between deposited and qFit-ligand 'B' conformers. Despite this, 17 structures had higher RSCC, 15 had higher EDIAm, 13 had lower strain, and 12 had both higher RSCC and lower strain in qFit-ligand models.
evaluation: Claims C80-C86 show mixed results for fragments. While map-to-model fit metrics improved in most cases, the algorithm struggled to recapitulate deposited conformers (only 45% with RMSD <0.5 Å). The authors acknowledge that ~33% of failures involved completely different binding poses that the algorithm cannot capture due to reliance on the input model (C81, C92-C94). The small sample size (n=20) limits generalizability.

result: For cryo-EM structures (n=4), qFit-ligand identified a second conformation in all cases, with improvements in RSCC (up to 0.1), EDIAm (up to 0.2), and strain reduction (up to 2.3 kcal/mol) compared to modified single-conformer models.
evaluation: Claims C87-C91 show consistent improvements across all four cryo-EM structures, but the extremely small sample size (n=4) severely limits the ability to draw general conclusions. The authors appropriately note this needs examination with a larger dataset. The proof-of-principle is demonstrated, but broader validation is required.

result: qFit-ligand is limited by reliance on the initial single-conformer structure, performs best with subtle conformational changes (torsion angles, minor translations), and struggles with dramatic conformational heterogeneity such as 180° ligand flips.
evaluation: Claims C92-C94 accurately describe acknowledged limitations supported by the fragment dataset results (C80-C81) showing difficulty with large conformational changes. The authors transparently discuss these limitations and their mechanistic basis (bias toward starting model). This is appropriately characterized as a limitation rather than a failure.

result: Approximately one-third of macrocycle datasets failed in standard preparation or post-refinement pipelines due to ligand parameterization issues, with many failures stemming from problematic ligand restraint files.
evaluation: Claims C95-C96 are supported by the quantitative observations from macrocycle dataset processing (C71-C73 showing ~51% total attrition). This highlights broader limitations in current refinement infrastructure for complex ligands rather than qFit-ligand specifically, which the authors appropriately acknowledge.

result: qFit-ligand operates on up to five CPU cores with typical runtimes under 10 minutes for 70.6% of ligands (mean: 8.6 min, median: 6.1 min), showing a strong correlation (Pearson r=0.75) between ligand size and runtime.
evaluation: Claims C41-C43 provide specific performance metrics with appropriate statistical measures. The correlation analysis is properly quantified and visualized (Figure 1—figure supplement 2). These computational performance characteristics are important for practical application.

result: From an initial collection of 2,199 PDB structures with multiconformer ligands, filtering yielded 1,534 structures, from which 135 were selected as a development set after manual inspection, with qFit-ligand modeling alternative conformations in 72.5% of these.
evaluation: Claims C44-C47 describe the dataset curation process with clear numbers at each filtering step. The manual inspection step (removing 15/150 structures where conformations didn't fit density well) demonstrates appropriate quality control. The 72.5% success rate in the development set provides context for the algorithm's performance.

result: qFit-ligand is restricted to output a maximum of three conformations for X-ray data and two conformations for cryo-EM data.
evaluation: Claims C38-C39 describe methodological constraints built into the algorithm. These are clearly stated design choices, though the rationale for the different limits between X-ray and cryo-EM is not explicitly justified in the manuscript.

result: RSCC values exceeding 0.80 indicate satisfactory agreement between model and experimental data.
evaluation: Claim C57 cites established standards (Smart et al., 2018; Shao et al., 2022) for RSCC interpretation. This is a standard metric in the field and is appropriately referenced.

result: Ligands exhibit diverse conformations in solution, with reduced diversity upon protein binding, though some flexibility is retained. A small number of PDB ligands are modeled with alternative conformations, while most are fit to single conformations potentially ignoring heterogeneity.
evaluation: Claims C1-C5 establish the scientific context and motivation for the work. These are supported by established knowledge (C1-C3), citations (C2, C4), and the dataset of 2,199 multiconformer ligands (C4) representing a small fraction of total PDB ligands (C5).

result: The prior version of qFit-ligand used iterative sampling over torsional degrees of freedom, which overlooked correlated motions, over-explored energetically unfavorable conformations, and could not model complex ligands like macrocycles.
evaluation: Claims C6-C7 and C23-C24 describe limitations of the prior version, supported by citations (C23) and comparative data showing the new version reduces strain in 68.9% of structures (C54). The inability to model macrocycles is addressed by successful modeling in the new version (C74-C77).

result: qFit-ligand has been extended to work with PanDDA-modified density maps from fragment screening and single-particle cryo-EM density maps, addressing the growth in these experimental approaches.
evaluation: Claims C10-C11 and C33-C36 describe methodological extensions supported by experimental demonstrations (fragment screening: C80-C86; cryo-EM: C87-C91). The context about growth in these methods is supported by citations (C33-C36).

result: X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM generate averaged datasets from thousands of system copies, encompassing significant conformational and compositional heterogeneity. Ligand modeling is challenging due to this heterogeneity, but proper multiconformer modeling can reveal biological function and guide drug design.
evaluation: Claims C16-C21 establish the scientific rationale for the work through established knowledge (C16) and appropriate citations (C17-C21). These provide important context for why multiconformer ligand modeling matters.

result: qFit uses mixed integer quadratic programming (MIQP) to optimize selection of a parsimonious set of conformers with corresponding occupancies.
evaluation: Claim C22 describes the core algorithmic approach, properly cited (van den Bedem et al., 2009) and detailed in the methods section with mathematical formulations.

result: Macrocycles (cyclic molecules ≥12 atoms) can interact with flat surfaces or shallow grooves, but their cyclic nature made modeling flexibility with the prior qFit-ligand approach troublesome.
evaluation: Claims C30-C32 provide context for macrocycle modeling. The definition (C30) and properties (C31) are well-cited. The difficulty with the prior approach (C32) is inferred from the inability to handle macrocycles and successful modeling in the new version.

result: High ligand strain is energetically unfavorable and reduces overall binding affinity.
evaluation: Claim C66 is supported by appropriate citations (Smola et al., 2021; Jain et al., 2023) and provides important context for why strain reduction is a meaningful metric.
